objective: 0.3.0 pi 3/10: Produce the Pi variant of the root and specialist instruction text and the eighteen role prompts, so a Pi agent receives the same rules as the Claude agents.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "please add intents for the next 0.3.0 release where I will implement the pi extension integration"; the maintainer implements 0.3.0, so these Intents record the work and carry no Assignments until the maintainer starts it.
Maintainer (verbatim): "in the docs/pi/ it's supposed to use already existent extensions for required functionality" and "the first provider to implement will be kimi for coding global".

Release model: work lands on release/0.3.0/integration cut from main, as one release/0.3.0/<type>/<change> branch and one PR per change; the first PR of the release carries the version bump made with mise run bump:minor.
Done means mise run verify passes with the generated output in sync (mise run build) and CI green on every required check, including the windows job.

Host-specific words in the root text are rewritten once in one Pi variant: Claude tool names become Pi tool names, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} becomes the Pi package install path, T3 Code tools are named only as optional, the scratchpad becomes the system temp area.
The Pi variant of specialist.md drops the sentence that AGENTS.md is not loaded, because Pi loads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md from the agent directory, the working directory and its parents.

Each of the eighteen specialists gets one prompt file (role text, specialist text, writing-bar for Worker.implementation and Reviewer.artifact, vendored frontend-design text with its LICENSE for the two visual roles) for use as the --append-system-prompt file of a spawned process.
The root text reaches Pi as system-prompt text through --append-system-prompt or APPEND_SYSTEM.md, never as a transcript message. Open: which of the two carriers.

Each role's tools are the allowlist the route table gives (read-only roles: read, grep, find, ls; Worker.operations and Worker.validation: bash but not write or edit; Reviewer.code keeps bash; Librarian roles get the web tool of the tool-surface Intent).
The package ships the dev-server and user-busy skills in the Agent Skills format; folded skills, the mergeability rubric, interface inspection rules and frontend-design text stay fixed role text.

The package ships code-review and security-review prompt templates in prompts/, which Reviewer.code and Reviewer.security expand as their first pass over the committed range. Open: the text of the two first-pass prompts, which the research does not give.
No path-guard extension is loaded, the version-control boundary stays instruction-only, no autoCompactWindow equivalent is set, no session_before_compact handler is registered.
The instruction files follow the cache requirements: static material first, no dates or counters, no mid-session roster change.

Open: which Pi model ids and thinking levels stand for the route table's haiku/sonnet, medium/high/xhigh and the root's opus; the first answer is for Kimi for Coding and is decided in the provider Intent.
Maintainer (verbatim): "for the pi integration we will need kimi k3.1 specific instructions following its official instruction guide".

The Pi instruction text has a Kimi K3.1 variant, a per-model set beside packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5 (for example kimi-k3.1/), written to Moonshot's official Kimi K3.1 prompting and instruction guide rather than adapted from the Claude 5.5 wording; each rule that departs from the Claude set cites the guide section it follows, the way the Claude set cites Anthropic's guidance.

Open: the official Kimi K3.1 instruction guide's URL and version, and which of its recommendations (system prompt structure, tool-use format, thinking mode, length and temperature defaults) apply to the root and to each specialist.
